record.title: Eleventh Circuit Holds Boca Raton and Palm Beach County Conversion-Therapy Ordinances Violate the First Amendment
record.description_short: A divided Eleventh Circuit panel held that conversion-therapy ordinances in Boca Raton and Palm Beach County violated the First Amendment.
record.description_medium: On November 20, 2020, a divided Eleventh Circuit panel ruled in Otto v. City of Boca Raton that ordinances in Boca Raton and Palm Beach County restricting licensed therapists from providing sexual-orientation-change counseling to minors violated the First Amendment. The court treated the rules as content-based speech regulations that failed strict scrutiny. Judge Beverly Martin dissented.
record.description_long: On November 20, 2020, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit decided an appeal by licensed therapists Robert Otto and Julie Hamilton challenging ordinances adopted by the City of Boca Raton and Palm Beach County. The local rules restricted licensed therapists from providing sexual-orientation-change counseling to minors. The City’s ordinance exempted clergy and allowed supportive counseling for people undergoing gender transition. The majority held that the ordinances regulated speech based on its content and could not survive strict scrutiny under the First Amendment. It reversed the district court’s denial of a preliminary injunction and remanded for entry of an injunction consistent with the opinion. Judge Beverly Martin dissented, arguing that the ordinances regulated professional conduct. The ruling concerned those two local ordinances and the therapists’ preliminary-injunction appeal; it did not announce a nationwide policy. The official opinion identifies the panel as Martin, Britt Grant, and Barbara Lagoa.
